gaps: No Korean food at all — a rich, tested cuisine completely absent from the collection.
No Japanese food — the wok and Dutch oven sit idle for an entire cuisine.
No egg-forward main dishes despite eggs being a vegetarian anchor protein.
No fish or seafood in any format — a full protein category missing.
The Ooni pizza oven appears in the equipment list but has never been used for a recipe.
No Middle Eastern food that goes beyond pantry-staple spicing — lentils, proper rice pilaf technique absent.
Weekend projects are thin — the Big Green Egg has no low-and-slow recipe to justify it.
Legume variety is narrow: chickpeas and white beans only; lentils entirely absent.

ideas.title: Dakgalbi (Spicy Stir-Fried Chicken and Vegetables)
ideas.why: Opens Korean cuisine from scratch using the carbon steel wok, a technique and cuisine entirely absent from the collection.

ideas.title: Mujaddara (Rice and Lentils with Crispy Onions)
ideas.why: Fills the lentil gap and the proper-Middle-Eastern gap in one shot; entirely vegetarian and deeply tested.

ideas.title: Shakshuka (Eggs in Spicy Tomato and Roasted Red Pepper Sauce)
ideas.why: Closes the egg-forward main gap with a one-skillet dish that works for the vegetarian adult without any modification.

ideas.title: Miso Salmon (Sake Misoyaki)
ideas.why: Introduces Japanese cuisine and fish in a format the family will eat — broiled fillets with no skin, no tacos.

ideas.title: Neapolitan-Style Pizza Dough
ideas.why: Finally deploys the Ooni; a proper 00-flour cold-ferment dough gives this experienced cook a genuine weekend project with a payoff the whole family can customize.

ideas.title: Texas-Style Smoked Brisket
ideas.why: Gives the Big Green Egg its first real low-and-slow project; beef brisket (not a chop, not lamb) fits the household's stated meat preferences perfectly.
